extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, administrative law practitioners, federal policymakers, judges, and regulated parties/public
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory standards and procedural requirements for Federal administrative agencies governing rulemaking, publication, adjudication (hearing commissioners), delegations, and declaratory rulings as set out in the Administrative Procedure Act (H.R. 184 / Public Law 404).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of general policy (Sec. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exercise of all administrative powers, insofar as they affect private rights, privileges, or immunities, should be effected by established procedures designed to assure the adequate protection of private interests and to effectuate the declared policies of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should be adapted to the necessities and differences of legislation and subject matter; must be made known to all interested persons. Administrative adjudication should assure due notice, adequate opportunity to present and meet evidence and argument, and prompt decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: agency and agency tribunal (Sec. 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Agency’ means any department, board, commission, authority, corporation, administration, independent establishment, or other subdivision of the executive branch empowered by law to determine rights, duties, immunities, or privileges of persons other than employees by rules/regulations or adjudications unreviewable except by courts. 'Agency tribunal' means the officer or group of officers within an agency whose adjudicative decisions are unreviewable except by the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine the scope of the Act's provisions and to whom publication, rulemaking, adjudication, and related duties apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority (Sec. 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency or agency tribunal may delegate to responsible members/officers/employees power to manage internal affairs, dispose informally of requests/complaints/applications/cases, issue complaints or show-cause orders, and govern preliminary/initial/intermediate/ancillary procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegations are subject to such supervision, direction, review, or reconsideration as the agency may prescribe. Multi-member tribunals may delegate deciding cases after hearing or on appeal to one or more members, subject to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel (Sec. 104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person appearing or summoned in any administrative proceeding shall be allowed the assistance of counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit right in administrative proceedings; agencies must permit counsel participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and powers of Office of Federal Administrative Procedure (Sec. 105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of a Director of Federal Administrative Procedure (seven-year term) and an Office composed of the Director, a D.C. Circuit justice designated by its chief justice, and the Director of the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts; Director may appoint necessary staff without regard to civil-service laws and fix compensation within Classification Act limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director authorized to appoint executive secretary, attorneys, investigators, experts, and other employees; central office to oversee uniformity and agency practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committees and agency cooperation (Sec. 106)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall designate administrative establishments as agencies; each such agency shall name an adviser to the Office; Director may constitute advisory committees from these representatives and add other officers or public members; agencies must promptly furnish requested information and assist the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may utilize agency personnel/facilities with consent; advisory mechanism to foster coordination and uniform practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the Director (Sec. 107)
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall conduct inquiries into agency practices/procedures to secure just and efficient discharge, make recommendations to facilitate uniform adoption of satisfactory methods, receive and investigate complaints about agency procedure, examine publicity practices, recommend rules regarding subpoenas/transcripts/testimony/documentary evidence/standards of proof/requests for findings, investigate admission to practice before agencies, perform duties related to appointment/removal of hearing commissioners, and transmit an annual report to President and Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual report must include names/qualifications of hearing commissioners appointed and circumstances of removal proceedings; Director has investigatory and recommendatory authority to standardize procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of rules and agency information (Sec. 201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall promptly make available and currently maintain a statement of its internal organization as it affects the public (officers, personnel types, subdivisions, places of business, duties, functions, authority/jurisdiction). All general policies and interpretations of law adopted, rules, regulations, procedures (formal or informal), prescribed forms and instructions with respect to reports or material required to be filed shall be made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires transparency about internal structure and public access to policies, interpretations, rules, and forms to enable informed dealings with agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation of rules: designated units to receive suggestions (Sec. 202)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall designate one or more units, committees, boards, officers, or employees to receive suggestions and expedite the making, amendment, or revision of rules, subject to agency control and supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates internal mechanism for handling rulemaking suggestions and for more responsive rule development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of rules — 45-day delay unless certified (Sec. 203)
rubrics_metrics.description: No regulation promulgated by an agency shall take effect until 45 days after initial publication in the Federal Register unless the regulation or authorizing statute provides a longer period; this limitation may be reduced or eliminated by certification published with the regulation that circumstances require an advanced effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a default notice period to allow public awareness and opportunity to respond, with emergency/required-advance exceptions via agency certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal petitions for regulations (Sec. 204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file with an agency a petition requesting the promulgation or amendment of a rule in which the petitioner has an interest; such petitions shall be submitted in form and with content as prescribed by each agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a statutory route for public-initiated rulemaking petitions; agencies may set procedural requirements for petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports to Congress about promulgated rules (Sec. 205)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annually each agency shall transmit all rules promulgated during the preceding 12 months with explanatory material relating to substance or procedure, and include a summary of formal requests for regulations received under section 204 and reasons for refusal of any such requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes reporting obligations to ensure Congressional oversight and transparency about rulemaking and refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and exceptions for administrative adjudication (Sec. 301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 302 to 309 apply only to proceedings where rights/duties/legal relations are required by law to be determined after opportunity for hearing and, if a hearing is held, only upon a record made in the hearing. They do not apply to certain proceedings: hearings before agency tribunals or individual members thereof, proceedings before state officers, proceedings preceding issuance of rules involving future governance of nonparty persons, military procurement/selection matters, personnel matters regarding U.S. employees (other than hearing commissioners), and matters relating to patent or trademark laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the boundaries of the adjudication provisions and enumerates specific statutory exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment, terms, removal, salaries, provisional/temporary appointment of hearing commissioners (Sec. 302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall appoint hearing commissioners as necessary; where five or more are appointed one is designated chief. Salaries specified ($7,500; $8,500 for chief; lower salary for uncomplicated cases when certified). Hearing commissioners may be selected without regard to civil service laws, nominated by the agency and appointed by the Office if qualified by training/experience/character. Nominations/appointments must be on basis of merit and efficiency, not political tests. Term: seven years; removable only on specified charges (malfeasance/neglect/inefficiency) or upon Attorney General charges, or certification of lack of business or appropriations. Provisional appointments up to one year (removable at agency discretion); temporary appointments for specific cases or up to 30 days under conditions (volume, vacancy, insufficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes independence protections, merit selection, fixed terms, limited removal grounds, pay levels, and mechanisms for provisional/temporary staffing to handle case loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing of cases (Sec. 303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, every case shall be heard before one or more hearing commissioners. Cases where facts are agreed need not be presented for hearing if agency tribunal directs. Agencies are not required to hold hearings when parties fail to answer a complaint or to appear when duly notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the default rule that cases get hearings before hearing commissioners but allows for agreed facts and default procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of hearing commissioner at hearing (Sec. 304(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing commissioner may administer oaths/affirmations and take affidavits; issue subpoenas for attendance/testimony and production of books/documents/evidence; examine witnesses and receive evidence; cause testimony to be taken by deposition; regulate proceedings subject to agency tribunal rules and take measures necessary for efficient conduct; exclude immaterial, irrelevant, unduly repetitious, or unreliable evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants broad factfinding and case-management powers, including evidentiary control and contempt referral for disobedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disobedience and contempt procedure (Sec. 304(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person in proceedings before a hearing commissioner disobeys lawful order/process, refuses to appear after subpoena, refuses oath, or refuses to be examined, the agency shall certify facts to the district court which shall promptly hear evidence and may order compliance or punish as for contempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides enforcement mechanism via courts for noncompliance with administrative subpoena/orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conferences and case management topics (Sec. 304(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing commissioners may initiate/conduct/participate in prehearing proceedings aimed at informal settlement or disposition; may direct parties to appear to consider simplification of issues, necessity/desirability of amendments to pleadings, obtaining stipulations of fact/documents to avoid unnecessary proof, limitation of number of expert witnesses, and other matters aiding disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages active case management to streamline hearings, limit costs, and focus issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing commissioner's decision: findings, briefs, oral argument, and written decisions (Sec. 304(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: After evidence, parties shall have opportunity to request findings of fact and conclusions of law, file briefs or argue orally per agency rules. The hearing commissioner shall find facts, formulate conclusions of law, and enter a decision stated in writing, served on parties, reported to the agency tribunal and included in the record; the commissioner may announce decision orally on the record and is required to provide fuller written findings only if requested by a party or agency tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedural protections around decisions, availability of written findings, and the record of decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers and duties of chief hearing commissioner (Sec. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief hearing commissioner has powers of hearing commissioners and duties including assigning commissioners to cases; certifying need for temporary commissioners due to accumulation/urgency; certifying extension of temporary designations; assigning another commissioner when original cannot complete hearing; directing issuance of findings/decisions by a different commissioner when necessary, with provision for reargument or retrial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides administrative oversight to manage workload and ensure continuity of proceedings and decision issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification procedure for hearing commissioners (Sec. 306)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may file a timely affidavit of disqualification with the chief hearing commissioner setting grounds with particularity. After hearing/investigation the chief shall find the affidavit without merit and direct case to proceed or assign another commissioner. If found without merit, affidavit and related records become part of the case record. A hearing commissioner shall withdraw when he deems himself disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a process for addressing alleged impartiality or disqualification with record-making requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: When no decision by hearing commissioner is required (Sec. 307)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon conclusion of hearing the hearing commissioner may certify novel or complex questions to the agency tribunal for binding instructions or transmission of the record. The agency tribunal may, on petition by any private party and for good cause, direct transmission of the entire record for its consideration. Parties have opportunity to request findings and present briefs or oral argument before the tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits agency tribunals to decide complex legal questions or take the case up on petition, preserving party participation rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of hearing commissioner's decision and reopening (Sec. 308)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent timely appeal to the agency tribunal, a hearing commissioner's decision becomes the final decision of the agency tribunal and is enforceable/reviewable as if duly entered by the tribunal; the agency head may on its own motion direct review after notice within prescribed period. The agency tribunal may reopen and alter/modify/set aside any unappealed final decision to the same extent it could its own final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates finality subject to appeal or agency-initiated review, and a mechanism for agency reopening of finalized hearing-commissioner decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of hearing commissioner's decision by agency tribunal on appeal (Sec. 309)
rubrics_metrics.description: On appeal the appellant must set forth with particularity each asserted error; only specified questions and portions of record need be considered. If appellant alleges findings are against the weight of the evidence, agency may limit inquiry to whether cited portions show findings clearly against weight of evidence. Agency tribunal shall afford reasonable opportunity to submit argument and may remand for further evidence/findings, or affirm, reverse, modify, set aside in whole or part, or itself make findings proper on the record. If tribunal findings differ materially from hearing commissioner’s, tribunal must file a statement explaining grounds with references to the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of appellate review within the agency and imposes a duty to explain material departures from hearing commissioner's findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record on appeal to courts (Sec. 310)
rubrics_metrics.description: In judicial review proceedings it is not necessary to print the complete record/exhibits unless court orders. Moving party shall print pertinent pleadings, orders, decisions, opinions, findings, conclusions of both agency tribunal and hearing commissioner, relevant docket entries arranged chronologically, and other portions desired for court to read; omissions indicated and transcript page references provided; responding party shall similarly print additional portions it desires the court to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to limit the burden of printing full records while ensuring courts have pertinent materials; courts may amplify or modify these provisions by rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake of remedy not to preclude judicial review (Sec. 311)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an order/determination is subject to judicial review but by a procedure or before a court different from that chosen by the person seeking review, the court may, instead of denying relief, proceed as if proper remedy had been sought, permit or direct amendment/rehearing/remand, or permit transfer to a court having jurisdiction, on such conditions as it deems just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides equitable remedies to avoid denying review due to procedural mischoice by a litigant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority to make rules to carry out the title (Sec. 313)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall have authority from time to time to make, amend, and rescind such rules and regulations as may be necessary to carry out the provisions of Title III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empowers agencies to adopt implementing procedures to comply with adjudication provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to issue declaratory rulings and limits (Sec. 401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency tribunal shall have power to issue declaratory rulings concerning rights, status, and other legal relations arising under statutes committed to its administration or under its regulations in order to terminate controversy or remove uncertainty. The tribunal may refuse to render a declaratory ruling where the ruling would not terminate the uncertainty, would be of uncertain future application, is sought for purpose of delay, would impede determination of other pending proceedings, or would be premature or otherwise inexpedient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants declaratory authority but lists discretionary grounds to refuse issuing rulings to prevent misuse or premature/uncertain pronouncements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of declaratory rulings (Sec. 402)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaratory ruling issued by an agency tribunal shall, in the absence of reversal after appropriate judicial proceedings, have the same force and effect and be binding in the same manner as a final order or other determination of that agency tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaratory rulings bind parties similarly to final orders unless reversed by a court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties in declaratory proceedings (Sec. 403)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a declaratory ruling is sought, all persons shall be made parties who have or claim any legal interest which would be affected by the declaration, and no declaration shall prejudice the rights of persons not parties to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures interested stakeholders are joined and protects nonparties from prejudicial effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review of declaratory rulings and refusal (Sec. 404)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review of a declaratory ruling may be had in the manner and to the same extent as final orders/determinations of that agency tribunal. Refusal to render a declaratory ruling shall not be subject to review in any manner. This title shall not modify existing law regarding closing agreements in internal revenue tax matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaratory rulings are reviewable like final agency decisions; agency refusals to rule are unreviewable.
